Display covr results using a standalone report

Source: R/report.R
report.Rd

report() saves the coverage report as a standalone HTML file and opens it. To include the report in a larger document, such as an R Markdown or Quarto document, use report_html() instead.

Usage

report(
  x = package_coverage(),
  file = file.path(tempdir(), paste0(get_package_name(x), "-report.html")),
  browse = interactive()
)

Arguments

x

a coverage dataset, defaults to running package_coverage().

file

The report filename.

browse

whether to open a browser to view the report.

Value

report() returns the absolute path of the report file, invisibly.

Branches

If branch coverage was measured with options(covr.branch_coverage = TRUE) (see covr.branch_coverage), the report also shows the branches of each if and switch(). The title has the percentage of branches taken after the line coverage, and the list of files has a "Branches" column with the percentage of the branches of each file that were taken. In the source, a line with branches has the number of its branches taken out of the total, e.g. 1/2; hovering over it or focusing it shows the label and count of each branch. A line with a branch that wasn't taken is shown as partly covered, unless its if or switch() never ran, which leaves it missed.

Colors

Covered lines are shown in green and missed lines in red. To use other colors, set the covr.report_colors option to a named character vector of R colors (anything accepted by grDevices::col2rgb(); transparency is ignored) with elements covered, missed and/or partial. The colors are used for the highlighted lines and the coverage bars in the file list; partial is used for the bars of files with at least 75% but less than 90% coverage, which otherwise follow covered, and for the partly covered lines of reports with branches, which are otherwise yellow.

colorblind_palette has colors that are easier to tell apart with color vision deficiency:

options(covr.report_colors = covr::colorblind_palette)

Dark mode

The report uses a dark theme if the browser or operating system is set to prefer one. The moon (or sun) button at the top right switches between the light and dark themes; the browser remembers the choice for other reports until it is switched back.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
x <- package_coverage()
report(x)

# Colors that are distinguishable with most kinds of color blindness
old <- options(covr.report_colors = colorblind_palette)
report(x)
options(old)
} # }
